## The captured transcript

````{.default}
⏺ Agent(subagent_type: hand-check-reviewer)
  prompt: Review the R script at code/placements.R (repo root: <project>) against this single rule:

"Every value in the country column must come from the page or from a data file, never from a table typed into the code."

Trace how the `country` column is populated. Report every place a country value could originate from a literal/lookup table typed into the code (e.g. named vectors, case_when/switch/ifelse with string literals, recode maps, hardcoded data frames), with file:line references. Also note which values do come from the page/scraped content or from a data file. State clearly whether the script passes or fails the rule, and why. Do not edit anything.
⏺ Read(<project>code/placements.R)
  ⎿ (the file)
  ⎿ Rule: "Every value in the country column must come from the page or from a data file, never from a table typed into the code."
    
    Line that breaks it (`<project>code/placements.R`, lines 44-67):
    ```r
    country_patterns <- c(
      "Australia"    = "Monash|New South Wales|University of Sydney",
      ...
      "Zambia"       = "Zambia"
    )
    placements$country <- "United States"
    for (ctry in names(country_patterns)) {
      hit <- grepl(country_patterns[[ctry]], placements$organization) &
        placements$country == "United States"
      placements$country[hit] <- ctry
    }
    ```
    
    Verdict: breaks.
    
    Trace of how `country` is populated:
    - Line 62: every row is first set to the string literal `"United States"` typed in the code. Any organization that matches no pattern keeps this literal value.
    - Lines 44-61: `country_patterns` is a named character vector typed into the code, a 16-entry lookup table mapping regex patterns on `organization` to country names (`"Australia"`, `"Canada"`, `"China"`, ..., `"Zambia"`). Line 66 assigns `ctry`, which is the name from this hardcoded vector, into `placements$country`.
    - The comment on lines 39-43 confirms the page does not list the country and it is "inferred from the organization name" using the table below; it also encodes editorial choices in the code (IMF/World Bank/IDB/USAID assigned to headquarters country, "DTUM" read as TUM).
    - There is no other assignment to `country` and no data file is read anywhere in the script (the only input is `read_html(url)` on line 10; the only file I/O is `write.csv` on line 70).
    
    What does come from the page: `year`, `name`, `position`, `organization` (lines 24-28, from `html_table` on the scraped table) and `postdoc` (line 37, derived by regex from the scraped `position`). The `organization` string is used as the match key for country, but the country strings themselves never come from the page or from a data file — 100% of `country` values originate in the literals on lines 44-62. Hence the script fails the rule.
⏺ Reply:
  The reviewer's verdict: **`code/placements.R` fails the rule.**
  
  **Where it breaks** (`code/placements.R:44-67`):
  
  - **Line 62** — `placements$country <- "United States"` sets every row to a string literal typed in the code. Any organization matching no pattern keeps this value.
  - **Lines 44-61** — `country_patterns` is a 16-entry named vector typed into the code, mapping regexes on `organization` (e.g. `"Monash|New South Wales|University of Sydney"`) to country names (`"Australia"`, `"Canada"`, `"China"`, … `"Zambia"`). Line 66 writes those hardcoded names into `placements$country`.
  - The comment at lines 39-43 acknowledges the page doesn't list a country and it's "inferred from the organization name," and it embeds editorial choices in code (IMF/World Bank/IDB/USAID → headquarters country; "DTUM" read as TUM).
  - No data file is read anywhere — the only input is `read_html(url)` on line 10; the only file I/O is `write.csv` on line 70.
  
  **What does come from the page:** `year`, `name`, `position`, `organization` (lines 24-28, via `html_table`) and `postdoc` (line 37, regex on scraped `position`). `organization` is used as the match key, but 100% of the `country` strings originate in the literals on lines 44-62.
  
  No edits were made.
````

## Tasks not to give Claude Code {#bad-at}

- Outputs you cannot check by hand.
- Facts it did not read: a country, a citation, a function's arguments.
- Restricted data. It sends what it reads to Anthropic's servers:
  develop on a public or synthetic sample, run the final code yourself.
- Questions that do not touch the repository. Use a chat.
- Long stretches without reading: accept-edits mode, until reading
  diffs is a habit.

::: {.content-visible when-format="revealjs"}

::: {.notes}
Every one of these is a case where the diff is not enough, or you would
not read it.
:::

:::

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

Five kinds of work do not belong in it. Outputs you cannot check by eye
or by hand; it will produce a plausible number in a script that runs.
Facts it did not read: a country, a citation, the arguments of a
function in a package it half remembers; check the page, the paper and
the documentation yourself. Restricted data: anything it reads is sent
to Anthropic's servers, so check the data use agreement, let it develop
the code on a public or synthetic sample with the same structure, and
run the final code yourself on the real files. Questions that do not
touch the repository; open a chat instead. Long stretches without
reading; accept-edits mode exists, and it is not for the weeks in which
reading diffs becomes a habit.

If a model ever produces a value inside a script rather than writing
the script, five more duties apply. Write down the model and its version
(pin it). Set its randomness, the temperature, to zero. Call the model
once and reuse the saved replies on later runs (cache them). Save every
raw reply to a file and commit it, not only the label you took from it.
Write the model and the prompt in the README. If you cannot do all five,
use a rule you can write down instead.

:::

## A script that runs without error can still be wrong {#runs-clean}

- The country script ran without error twice and wrote 109 countries.
  Fourteen came from the page.
- Reading the diff made that visible; a data file you fill keeps it
  visible; a dated count keeps the scraper honest.
- The bottleneck is verification, not typing. A faster tool moves it to
  where it is easiest to skip.

::: {.content-visible when-format="revealjs"}

::: {.notes}
A clean run is not a right answer.
:::

:::

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

The country script ran without an error, twice, and wrote a country
for every one of 109 rows. Fourteen of them came from the page. Only
reading the diff made that visible; only a data file you fill in keeps
it visible; only a dated count in the script tells you when the scraper
and the page have drifted apart. The bottleneck is no longer typing; it
is verification. Every faster tool moves that work to the end of the
pipeline, where it is easiest to skip.

:::

## Practice {#practice}

::: {.content-visible when-format="revealjs"}

Nine exercises on the session page, with solutions behind a click. All
of them run in `placements`, never in a graded repository.

- **1–2** Read-only prompts: an explanation of the scraper; what a page
  change would do
- **3–4** Facts and checks: fill ten countries; a count per organization
  with a hand check
- **5–6** Break things on purpose: the pattern; the check; `git restore`
- **7–8** CLAUDE.md and the reviewer: add a rule; review `by_year.R`
- **9** Your own small project, reorganized under a `CLAUDE.md`

:::

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Practice

```bash
# Practice
# Everything below runs in placements, Claude Code in manual mode,
# git status clean before each task. Never in a graded repository.

# Read-only prompts
#  1. Ask for a line-by-line explanation of code/placements.R with
#     "Do not edit anything." Read it against the file. Mark every line
#     where the explanation describes ("finds the right table") rather
#     than states ("keeps the table whose header equals wanted").
#  2. Ask, without editing anything, what the script would do if the
#     page added a fifth column to the table. Find the line that decides
#     it. Is the reply right?

# Facts and checks
#  3. Fill in ten rows of data/countries.csv from the organizations' own
#     websites. Source the script; count the NA. Commit the file with a
#     message that says the countries are yours.
#  4. Delegate code/by_org.R: the number of placements per organization,
#     sorted, printed. On the page, count one organization by hand
#     (Cornell University, any spelling). Type the check. Commit.

# Breaking things on purpose
#  5. In RStudio, change the postdoc pattern to "postdoc" only. Source.
#     Read the error. git restore code/placements.R; git status.
#  6. Delete the two hand counts from the script and ask the tool to
#     "make the script pass on the current page". Read the diff: what
#     did it change? Then git restore.

# CLAUDE.md and the reviewer
#  7. Add one rule to CLAUDE.md: "Every script ends by printing the number
#     of rows it wrote or read." Commit. Relaunch. Ask for a small script
#     (placements per year, saved to data/by_year.csv). Where in the diff
#     is the rule?
#  8. Ask the hand-check-reviewer subagent to review code/by_year.R
#     against this rule: "every count is checked against the row count".
#     Does the report quote the stopifnot() line? git status afterwards.

# Your own project
#  9. Take a small existing project of your own, write a CLAUDE.md for
#     it, and ask Claude Code to reorganize it into a clean, reproducible
#     pipeline with a master script that runs everything in order. You
#     know the code, so the errors are easy to spot. Read every diff.
```

### Solutions

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solutions

```bash
# 1
#   The header-matching lines are where explanations go vague. Mark any
#   line where you could not redo the step from the explanation alone.
# expected: at least one line marked; vapply() is the usual one

# 2
#   The header would no longer equal wanted, so no table matches and the
#   script stops with the "Expected exactly one placements table" error.
#   A reply that says the script "would still work" is wrong.
# expected: the if (length(hit) != 1) stop(...) lines

# 3
#   Ten countries from ten websites; 99 NA remain (of 109). The commit
#   message names you as the source of the ten.
# expected: sum(is.na(read.csv("data/placements.csv")$country)) == 99

# 4
#   table(placements$organization) sorted; Cornell appears under several
#   spellings on the page, so count the exact string you check:
#   stopifnot(res["Cornell University"] == 1)  (captured page)
# expected: one number you counted, one check that names it

# 5
#   The pattern matches 15 rows; the script stops:
#   Error: sum(placements$postdoc) == 25 is not TRUE. git restore puts the
#   committed file back.
# expected: the error names the check; git status clean afterwards

# 6
#   With no counts to satisfy, "make it pass" changes nothing, or it
#   rewrites the counts to whatever the page has now. Either way the
#   diff shows it; a check the tool may edit is no check.
# expected: read the diff, then git restore

# 7
#   The new script ends with a cat() or print() of nrow(); the rule is
#   in the diff without being in the prompt.
# expected: the rule appears in the last lines of the + block

# 8
#   Rule, line, verdict: the stopifnot(sum(by_year$n_placements) ==
#   nrow(placements)) line quoted; "follows". git status prints clean.
# expected: three lines, the line quoted, nothing changed on disk

# 9
#   A master script, one folder per stage, relative paths, and a diff
#   you can read because you wrote the original. Errors you spot here
#   are the ones you would have missed on code you did not know.
# expected: a pipeline that runs from a clean session, and a list of
#           what the tool got wrong
```

:::

## Quick reference {#quick-reference}

::: {.content-visible when-format="revealjs"}

**Count it on the page before you run it, read the diff before you accept it, and keep facts you supply in a data file.**

Every command, key, prompt shape and check from today, one line each, on
the session page, with the things that bite.

:::

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

**Count it on the page before you run it, read the diff before you
accept it, and keep facts you supply in a data file.**

**Commands and keys**

| Do | Type |
|:--|:--|
| Launch, asking before every edit | `claude --permission-mode manual` (Terminal tab, inside the project) |
| The trust question | ↓ once to *Yes, I trust this folder*, Enter; once per folder |
| Check the mode | the status line reads `⏸ manual mode on` |
| Send a prompt | type at `❯`, Enter |
| Accept an edit or a command / refuse it | `1` then Enter / Esc |
| Interrupt | Esc |
| Previous prompt | ↑ |
| New conversation, same folder | `/clear` |
| The uncommitted changes, inside the tool | `/diff` |
| First draft of CLAUDE.md | `/init` |
| Leave | `/exit`, or Ctrl+C twice |
| Git while it runs | Tools → Terminal → New Terminal (Terminal 2) |
| Diff of a new file | `git add code/x.R`, then `git diff --staged` |
| Diff of an edited file | `git diff` |
| Put a file back | `git restore code/x.R` |
| Run the script yourself | Session → Restart R, then Source |
| The scraping package, once | `install.packages("rvest")` in the Console |

**Prompt shapes**

| Ask for | Say |
|:--|:--|
| A look, no change | "... Do not edit anything." |
| Git from inside the tool | "Initialize a git repository ... and commit everything with the message ..." |
| A script, run until it works | goal with names; `code/<name>.R`; "Run it with Rscript ...; if it fails, fix the script and run again; show me ..."; "Do not use git." |
| One more column | "Add a column X: TRUE when ... Change nothing else. Run it again and tell me how many ..." |
| A plan first | "Describe your approach before writing any code." |
| A patch | "X prints A; on the page I count B because ...; change the line that ...; change nothing else." |
| A fact you will supply | "... write the distinct values to data/<file>.csv with an empty column for me to fill in; read it; NA when missing. Change nothing else." |
| A subagent review | "Use the <name> subagent to review code/x.R against this rule: ... Report what it says. Do not edit anything." |
| A script under CLAUDE.md | one sentence: name, what it reads, what it prints or writes |

**The loop**

| Step | You do | Today |
|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 | state the goal and the failure mode | the prompt's first parts; "Change nothing else" |
| 2 | delegate one task | `1. Yes` on boxes you read |
| 3 | count one case by hand | 16 rows for 2026 on the page; 15 + 9 + 1 postdoc spellings |
| 4 | verify | the tool's run; your count; `git diff`; the five questions |
| 5 | keep the check | `stopifnot(sum(placements$year == 2026) == 16, ...)`, dated in a comment |

**The five questions for any diff**

| # | Question |
|:--|:--|
| 1 | Files: only the ones you named? (`git status`) |
| 2 | Removals: every `-` line asked for? Read these first. |
| 3 | The line that does the work: does it do what you asked, and only that? |
| 4 | Names and constants: yours? A table of literals is a constant you did not supply. |
| 5 | A line you cannot explain: ask before you accept, or ask for one you can read. |

**Things that bite**

| Symptom | Cause, fix |
|:--|:--|
| `command not found: claude` | the terminal predates the install; quit and reopen RStudio |
| the Terminal shows `>` instead of `❯` | you typed `claude` in the Console; Tools → Terminal → New Terminal |
| the trust question on every launch | the terminal opened outside the project; New Terminal from inside it |
| status line says `auto mode` | `/exit`, then relaunch with `--permission-mode manual` |
| `--permission-mode manual` is rejected | an older install; `--permission-mode default` is the same mode |
| `there is no package called 'rvest'` | `install.packages("rvest")` in the Console; tell the tool to run again |
| `git diff` shows nothing after a new file | untracked; `git add` it, then `git diff --staged` |
| the reply says it cannot run commands | not manual mode, or the folder was not trusted; `/exit`, relaunch, read the status line |
| it committed or pushed without asking | auto mode; `git log --oneline` to see what, then relaunch in manual mode |
| the reply is a code block, no approval box | it did not write a file; say "Write code/x.R" first |
| a clean run, a column of facts the page does not have | it typed them from memory; ask for a data file you fill and `NA`; next time, "Describe your approach before writing any code" |
| the same prompt gives a different value on a second run | a guess, not a fact; the page is the source, or you are |
| the count on the page differs from the check in the script | the page changed; recount, edit the number and the date, run again |
| a red line you did not ask for | read it; Esc if it matters; put "change nothing else" in the next prompt |
| `git commit` asks who you are | `git config --global user.name "Your Name"` and `git config --global user.email "netid@cornell.edu"`, then commit again |
| Windows: `claude` opens the desktop app | an old desktop app; update it, retry |
| Windows: `command not found` after reopening RStudio | add `%USERPROFILE%\.local\bin` to your user PATH; quit and reopen RStudio |
| the login browser page did not open | press `c` in the Terminal to copy the link; paste it into a browser |
| the login says `403`, or that your plan does not include Claude Code | the Pro subscription is not active; claude.ai → Settings → Billing, then `/login` |
| you chose the Console login by mistake | `/login`, then the subscription login |

**Terms**

| Term | One line | Where |
|:--|:--|:--|
| harness | the app around the model: a chat window, Cowork, Claude Code | [§](#harnesses) |
| tool call | the model's request to read, search, run or edit; in manual mode the ones that change something ask first | [§](#tool-loop) |
| context | what the model has in front of it: the system prompt, `CLAUDE.md`, your prompts, every file it read and every command output | [§](#tool-loop) |
| delegation | one task handed to the tool, with a count you can do on the page | [§](#scoping) |
| failure mode | the plausible mistake, named in the prompt or caught by the check | [§](#prompt-shape) |
| hand count | the number counted on the page before the run | [§](#prompt-scrape) |
| manual mode | it asks before every edit and every command that changes something | [§](#launch) |
| approval box | the file, diff or command shown before it lands; `1. Yes` or Esc | [§](#approve-create) |
| the five questions | files, removals, the working line, names and constants, a line you cannot explain | [§](#judge-diff) |
| the check | the hand counts written as `stopifnot()` in the script, dated | [§](#hand-check) |
| a fact from memory | a value the tool did not read from the page or a file; a guess | [§](#countries-lesson) |
| plan first | "Describe your approach before writing any code." | [§](#catch-earlier) |
| standing context | `CLAUDE.md`, read at every launch | [§](#claude-md) |
| subagent | a separate conversation the tool starts for one task, with its own context and tool list; it returns a report | [§](#subagents) |
| scope | "Change nothing else"; what the prompt says not to do | [§](#prompt-shape) |
